identity.title: A first look at the submillimeter Sun with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the first full-disk solar images obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) in Band 7 (0.86 mm; 347 GHz).

In order to accommodate for the flattening of the curve in Band 7, we used the following third degree fit: $$ egin{equation} T_b(\mu)=A_0+A_1\ln\mu+A_2\ln^2\mu+A_3\ln^3\mu \label{logmu0}, \end{equation}$$ rather than the linear fit used in previous works.

findings_qualitative.value: Quiet Sun chromospheric network structures in Band 7 (0.86 mm) show practically a one-to-one correspondence with AIA 1600/1700 Å and 304 Å images and negative H-alpha images smoothed to the ALMA resolution.

evidence.quote: Quiet Sun structures on the disk are similar to those in Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) images at 1600 Å and 304 Å, after the latter are smoothed to the ALMA resolution
We note that there is practically a one-to-one correspondence between the ALMA and the AIA network structures, as previously reported for Bands 6 and 3 by (cite: 2017A&A...605A..78A).

findings_qualitative.value: Polar coronal holes clearly seen at 304 Å and small H-alpha filaments are not detectable in Band 7 at 0.86 mm.

evidence.quote: Polar coronal holes, which are clearly seen in the 304 Å band and small H$\alpha$ filaments, are not detectable at 0.86 mm.

findings_qualitative.value: The combined T_b(log mu_100) curve and the inverted T_e(log tau_100) profile flatten at high frequencies / large optical depths, indicating that Band 7 observations approach the solar temperature minimum.

evidence.quote: More importantly, the $T_b(\log\mu_{100})$ curve flattens at large values of $\mu_{100}$, and so does the corresponding $T_e(\log	au_{100})$ at large $	au_{100}$. This is probably an indication that we are approaching the temperature minimum.

claims.hypothesis: Quiet Sun structures in ALMA Band 7 (0.86 mm) trace the chromospheric network similarly to UV/EUV and H-alpha diagnostics, while coronal holes and optically thin filaments are absent.
claims.experiment: Compare full-disk and central 500'' x 500'' ALMA Band 7 TP images against resolution-matched AIA 1600/1700 Å, AIA 304 Å, and GONG H-alpha images.
claims.result: One-to-one correspondence of network structures with AIA and negative H-alpha images; small active/plage regions are ~900 K brighter; polar coronal holes and three small H-alpha filaments have no counterpart in Band 7.
claims.finding: Band 7 quiet Sun emission closely matches chromospheric network structures seen in AIA 1600/1700/304 Å and negative H-alpha, whereas polar coronal holes and small H-alpha filaments are undetectable at 0.86 mm.

evidence.quote: Polar coronal holes, which are clearly seen in the 304 Å band and small H$\alpha$ filaments, are not detectable at 0.86 mm.
We note that there is practically a one-to-one correspondence between the ALMA and the AIA network structures, as previously reported for Bands 6 and 3 by (cite: 2017A&A...605A..78A).

claims.hypothesis: The central disk brightness temperature in Band 7 is higher than the 5500 K value extrapolated from recommended Band 3 and Band 6 values.
claims.experiment: Combine CLV measurements from Bands 3, 6, and 7 reduced to 100 GHz and normalize to December 2015 Band 3 commissioning observations via a third-degree polynomial least-squares fit.
claims.result: Derived disk-center T_b is 6085 K for Band 7 (10.6% above 5500 K) and 6347 K for Band 6 (7.6% above 5900 K), with fit rms of ~13 K.
claims.finding: Assuming accurate Band 3 commissioning calibration, the true central disk brightness temperature in Band 7 is 6085 K, confirming that both Band 6 and Band 7 exceed recommended/extrapolated values.

evidence.quote: Assuming that the absolute calibration of the Band 3 commissioning observations is accurate, we deduced a brightness temperature at the center of the disk of 6085 K for Band 7, instead of the value of 5500 K
The values for Bands 3 and 6 are very close to those given in Paper II, while the disk temperature for Band 7 is 6085 K, or 10.6% above the extrapolated recommended value of 5500 K.

claims.hypothesis: ALMA Band 7 observations probe deeper chromospheric layers approaching the temperature minimum.
claims.experiment: Fit the combined multi-band CLV curve T_b(ln mu_100) with a third-degree polynomial and analytically invert the radiative transfer equation to obtain T_e(ln tau_100).
claims.result: The Band 7 CLV slope is smaller than in Bands 3 and 6, causing both T_b(log mu_100) and T_e(log tau_100) to flatten at large mu_100 and tau_100 (with cubic fit coefficients a_0 = 6964, a_1 = -680, a_2 = 30, a_3 = 19).
claims.finding: The flattening of T_b(log mu_100) and T_e(log tau_100) at large optical depth is a plausible indication that Band 7 approaches the solar temperature minimum, though verification with more observations is needed.

evidence.quote: More importantly, the $T_b(\log\mu_{100})$ curve flattens at large values of $\mu_{100}$, and so does the corresponding $T_e(\log	au_{100})$ at large $	au_{100}$. This is probably an indication that we are approaching the temperature minimum.

It is quite plausible that this flattening is due to the fact that in Band 7, we approach the region of the temperature minimum. Still, this result relies on observations during a single day and needs verification with more data.

why_this_data.value: First full-disk solar observations in ALMA Band 7 (347 GHz) obtained in the same campaign as Bands 3 and 6 provide a homogeneous multi-frequency dataset without needing older 350 GHz literature data.

evidence.quote: With the present Band 7 observations, we have a homogeneous set of data at our disposal, which we subsequently exploit in this section in order to obtain more reliable results.
The present result is more reliable since we have a homogeneous data set and thus there was no need to resort to the old measurements of (cite: 1993ApJ...415..364B) at 350 GHz, as we had done before.

why_this_method.value: Combining multi-frequency CLV data via f^-2 opacity scaling and inverting T_b(mu) treats frequencies simultaneously, avoids primary beam effects near the limb, and yields T_e(tau) directly; CASA sdgaincal suppresses double-circle scan modulations.

evidence.quote: We were able to largely suppress them by invoking CASA’s task sdgaincal before mapping.

(a) data at different frequencies are treated simultaneously; (b) there is no need to go close to the limb, thus avoiding primary beam effects; and (c) it provides the physically meaningful quantity $T_e(	au)$ directly.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Comparing observed CLV curves at individual frequencies to curves computed from models or determining limb brightening coefficients

evidence.quote: We note that this approach has a number of advantages over the comparison of the CLV observed at various frequencies to curves obtained from models (cite: 2019ApJ...871...45S), or the determination of limb brightening coefficients (cite: 2019SoPh..294..163S)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Linear and quadratic fits to T_b(ln mu), rejected in favor of a third-degree polynomial fit due to higher rms deviations (26.6 K and 16.0 K vs 13 K) and the flattening in Band 7

evidence.quote: In order to accommodate for the flattening of the curve in Band 7, we used the following third degree fit: $$ egin{equation} T_b(\mu)=A_0+A_1\ln\mu+A_2\ln^2\mu+A_3\ln^3\mu \label{logmu0}, \end{equation}$$ rather than the linear fit used in previous works.
The root mean square (rms) deviation was about 13 K, whereas linear and quadratic fits gave rms deviations of 26.6 K and 16.0 K, respectively.

limitations_admitted.value: Absolute calibration jumps exist between datasets, and cross-normalization cannot replace true absolute calibration (e.g., using the Moon).

evidence.quote: As noted in Paper II, there is a jump in $T_b$ between the commissioning and the current Band 6 data set, attributed to absolute calibration issues, and so is the case with Band 7.
Reliable as this result may be, it cannot replace the imperative need for absolute calibration of ALMA solar observations, using the moon for example.

However, the diffuse light correction details are deferred to Paper I, the exact December 2015 commissioning dataset code is not stated, and the fitted normalization factors and CASA/sdgaincal parameters are omitted.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Total Power data (2019.1.01532.S) with a clear mathematical recipe for CLV frequency remapping, polynomial fitting, and analytical radiative transfer inversion yielding specific numeric disk-center brightness temperatures and atmospheric parameters.
